text:
Maria Chen: quick sync — we need to lock the apples-to-apples methodology for the model comparison doc. kernel selection + batching + kv warm/cold behaviour all need consistent rules. who can take point?
Ben Ortiz: I can draft. question: do we standardize on replay harness only or include synthetic traffic for specific microbenchmarks?
Maria Chen: both. replay for end-to-end, synthetic for isolating kernel/batching effects. but we must be explicit about seeding, stop sequences, tokenizer choices.
Jasper Li: +1. proposed flow:
1) tokenizer alignment pass (same tokenizer binary + version, ensure tokenization of prompts and stops identical)
2) deterministic decode params: temperature=0, top_p=1.0, max_new_tokens=128, penalty=0
3) two KV modes: cold (fresh process) and warm (prepopulated KV from 64-token prefix)
4) per-model kernel selection: record the kernel plan used (e.g., flash_attn_v2 / generic_attn) and pin if we want identical kernels across runs
Rachel K: add batching profile: run single-request latency (no batch), then throughput curve at batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16]. measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
Ben Ortiz: for replay harness: we should use 1M tokens worth of real traffic replayed across 20 clients to simulate concurrency. record sequence length distribution and use same random ordering for each model run.
Jasper Li: important: the replay harness must inject identical decoding termination (stop sequences) — if model B tokenizes stop differently we get different termination lengths. hence tokenizer alignment first.
Maria Chen: agreed. also note: when comparing quantized variants we must ensure kernel compatibility. otherwise perf differences mix quantization + kernel selection. we should have a kernel-locked experiment set.
Ben Ortiz: draft config snippet (python-like):
```
HARNESS = {
  "tokenizer": "tokenizers/v2.1.0/bin",
  "decode": {"temperature": 0, "top_p": 1.0, "max_new_tokens": 128},
  "stop_sequences": ["

"],
  "kv_modes": ["cold","warm"],
  "batch_sizes": [1,2,4,8,16],
  "replay_seed": 42,
  "replay_clients": 20
}
```
Rachel K: we should also capture low-level perf counters: GPU SM utilization, memory bw, PCIe stalls, kernel launch count. add nvprof/nvmetrics snapshots at p50 and p99 points.
Jasper Li: I ran a quick smoke yesterday to show why this matters. paste of trimmed log:
```
MODEL: open-llm-14B
KV_MODE: warm
BATCH: 8
p50_infer_ms: 122.3
p95_infer_ms: 310.7
p99_infer_ms: 745.2
KV_cache_hit_rate: 0.88
kernel_plan: flash_attn_v2 (selected)
note: bursty tail aligned with cache refill cycles
```
Ben Ortiz: interesting — on the same workload with a different kernel choice (generic_attn) we saw p99 jump to ~980ms and SM utilization dropped ~12%. that's likely due to different memory access pattern.
Maria Chen: action items: Ben to run full cross-model replay suite; Jasper to produce kernel-locked vs kernel-auto comparisons; Rachel to add telemetry checklists and dashboards. timeline?
Ben Ortiz: I can start the runs tonight, will upload results by EOD tomorrow.
Jasper Li: I'll prepare a script to force kernel selection and to collect kernel metadata from the runtime, example command:
```
rdw-run --model open-llm-14B --force-kernel flash_attn_v2 --profile nvmetrics --out /tmp/run1
```
Rachel K: added note — include token-level latency histograms and emit aggregated tokenization diffs (how many stops were split across tokens) so reviewers can sanity-check termination mismatch.
Maria Chen: perfect. one more thing: regression gating. if p99 increases by >15% for any critical route, auto-fail unless an owner signs off with explanation. put that in the doc.
perf-bot: rerun complete: 1776348200 | run_id=run-20260318-01 | model=open-llm-14B | kv=warm | batch=8 | p50=121.9 | p95=309.1 | p99=738.0
Ben Ortiz: perf-bot numbers look consistent with smoke. I'll attach full CSV and kernel selection logs when done.
Maria Chen: thanks everyone. once Ben's CSV and Jasper's kernel logs are in, I'll draft the apples-style comparison section showing side-by-side decode traces, token counts, and the kernel/kv/batching matrix. then we can share with product for perf claims. :thumbsup:
Rachel K: also flagging — if any model variant changes tokenizer behavior between versions, we must run a tokenizer-diff and fail the apples comparison until resolved.
Jasper Li: noted. I'll add a small unit test in the harness: run tokenization(prompt+stop) on both models' tokenizers and assert identical token sequences.
Maria Chen: excellent. closing loop — Ben, ping here when the first full-run CSV is uploaded.
Ben Ortiz: will do. thanks! :rocket:
